applicableAreas: Transformer Pad 1 west side near Building 2
Transformer Pad 2 west side near Building 8
findings.observation: Electrical design plan (Sheet 21) shows three transformer pads as dotted rectangles. Pads 1 and 2 are positioned on the west side of the site near Buildings 2 and 8 respectively, in proximity to the property line and sidewalk easement areas. Site plan (Sheet 9) shows general building layout but does not include dimensional clearance measurements between the transformer pads and building facades. Vision analysis confirms Pad 1 is positioned between Building 2 and the western property boundary (sidewalk area), and Pad 2 is positioned similarly near Building 8. However, no numerical measurements (e.g., "5 feet minimum") are provided on any submitted plan sheets to document actual clearances from building foundations or structures.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4 requires a minimum 5-foot clearance from pad-mounted equipment to buildings, structures, and building foundations. The applicant bears the burden of demonstrating compliance through documented measurements or calculations on the plans. While the plans show transformer pad locations and building positions, the absence of explicit clearance measurements between the pad edges and building walls prevents verification of compliance. This constitutes failure to document the required clearances, not merely unclear positioning. However, since the pads are shown at some distance from the buildings (not touching), the deficiency cannot be definitively proven as a pass or fail without actual measurements. This requires clarification through submission of dimensional drawings showing clearances.
findings.comment: Transformer pads shown on electrical design plan lack documented clearance measurements to adjacent buildings. Provide dimensioned drawings or calculations demonstrating minimum 5-foot clearance from edge of transformer pad to building foundations and exterior walls.

applicableAreas: Transformer Pad 1 near sidewalk easement
Transformer Pad 2 near sidewalk easement
findings.observation: Electrical design plan (Sheet 21) identifies sidewalk easement areas on the western edge of the property adjacent to Transformer Pads 1 and 2. Site plan (Sheet 9) shows sidewalk/pedestrian areas along Valley View Road. Grading plan (Sheet 11) indicates curb elevations and pedestrian access areas. Vision analysis of Sheet 21 confirms sidewalk easement marking near both western pads. However, no explicit measurements are provided documenting the distance from the back of the sidewalk to the transformer pad edges.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4 requires a minimum 2-foot clearance from the back of sidewalks. Sidewalk easements are clearly depicted on the electrical plan in proximity to Pads 1 and 2, but without dimensional documentation (measurements in feet) on the plans, the actual clearance cannot be verified. The pads appear to be positioned nearby the sidewalk area, but confirmation of the specific 2-foot minimum requires dimensioned drawings.
findings.comment: Transformer Pads 1 and 2 shown near sidewalk easements on electrical plan lack documented clearance measurements. Provide dimensioned drawings demonstrating minimum 2-foot clearance from back of sidewalk to edge of transformer pad.

applicableAreas: All three transformer pad locations
findings.observation: Electrical design plan (Sheet 21) shows three transformer pads as dotted rectangles but provides no indication of access door orientation or hot-stick use area boundaries. Site plan (Sheet 9) does not include transformer pad detail orientation information. Vision analysis of Sheet 21 confirms that pad access door orientation is not visible/marked on the submitted plans for any of the three pads.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4 requires minimum 10-foot clearance to open area or adjacent building/structure on the side where the hot-stick (access door) is located. Without knowing which side of each transformer pad contains the access door, it is impossible to verify whether the required 10-foot clearance exists in the appropriate direction. The plans must indicate access door orientation and the associated 10-foot use area to demonstrate compliance.
findings.comment: Transformer pad access door orientation not indicated on electrical design plan. Provide documentation showing which side of each transformer pad contains the access door and demonstrating minimum 10-foot clearance from the access door side to open area or adjacent structure.

applicableAreas: Transformer Pad 3 central location between Buildings 4, 5, and 6
findings.observation: Electrical design plan (Sheet 21) shows Transformer Pad 3 positioned centrally within the site, surrounded by Buildings 4 (north), 5 (east), and 6 (south) within a parking/circulation area. Site plan (Sheet 9) shows these buildings in close proximity to each other. Vision analysis of Sheet 21 notes that the central pad is "located within an open paved/drive area surrounded by three aforementioned buildings." No cross-section drawings are provided showing whether the pad access door faces any of these surrounding buildings or is within a confined space (niche, vault, or enclosed area on 3+ sides).
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4 requires minimum 15-foot clearance when the access door side faces a confined space (niche, vault, or enclosed area on 3 or more sides), compared to the standard 10-foot clearance for open areas. Transformer Pad 3's location between three buildings suggests it may face a confined space orientation on one or more sides. However, without access door orientation documentation and no cross-section drawings demonstrating the configuration, it cannot be determined whether the 15-foot confined space threshold applies or whether the applicable clearance requirement has been met.
findings.comment: Transformer Pad 3 located between multiple buildings in central courtyard area. Provide documentation clarifying whether the pad access door faces a confined space (3+ sides enclosed). If confined space applies, provide dimensioned drawings or cross-sections demonstrating minimum 15-foot clearance from access door.

applicableAreas: Transformer Pad 3 central location near fire hydrant
findings.observation: Utility plan (Sheet 19) identifies two fire hydrants: one at the site entrance (external, being replaced) and one internally located between Buildings 4 and 7. This internal fire hydrant is positioned in the central area where Transformer Pad 3 is also located. Electrical design plan (Sheet 21) shows Transformer Pad 3 in the same central courtyard area surrounded by Buildings 4, 5, and 6. Vision analysis of utility plan confirms the fire hydrant location marked with "FH" adjacent to Building 7. However, no dimensional clearance measurements are provided on any plan sheets documenting the distance between the transformer pad and the fire hydrant.
findings.reasoning: Site planning convention requires a minimum 5-foot clearance from transformer pads to fire hydrants to ensure hydrant accessibility and operation. While the site plans show both the fire hydrant and Transformer Pad 3 in the same general central area, no measurements are provided to verify the actual clearance distance. This prevents confirmation of compliance without dimensioned documentation.
findings.comment: Fire hydrant shown in central courtyard area near Transformer Pad 3. Provide dimensioned drawing documenting minimum 5-foot clearance from transformer pad edge to fire hydrant.

applicableAreas: Landscape areas along site perimeter with trees
findings.observation: Landscape plan (Sheet 31) shows numerous trees marked with symbols: SY (Street Yard), PL (Parking Lot), P (Parking Buffer), and M (Mitigation) distributed along the north, south, east, and west property boundaries. Vision analysis of Sheet 31 confirms trees are located in multiple areas including street yard (west side) and along all perimeter boundaries. Sheet 32 (Tree List) is referenced but not examined in detail. Electrical plan (Sheet 21) shows three transformer pads positioned within the development interior. However, the landscape plan does not include dimensioned measurements documenting distances between the proposed trees and transformer pad locations. Additionally, no cross-reference is provided between the landscape plant list and ECM Appendix F "UC" (Utility Compatible) column to verify species compatibility with utility infrastructure proximity.
findings.reasoning: The landscape plan identifies tree locations and provides symbols (SY, PL, P, M) indicating tree types and mitigation counts, but does not measure distances to transformer pad locations or confirm species utility compatibility. This prevents verification of compliance without additional detailed landscape documentation linking tree species to ECM Appendix F compatibility ratings and providing distance measurements from each proposed tree to the nearest transformer pad.
findings.comment: Landscape plan shows trees throughout the site but lacks dimensioned distances to transformer pads and species cross-reference to ECM Appendix F utility compatibility column. Provide detailed tree list with species identification cross-referenced to ECM Appendix F and distance measurements showing trees within 10 lateral feet of transformer pads are utility-compatible species.

applicableAreas: All proposed landscape trees within 20 lateral feet of transformer pad locations
findings.observation: Landscape plan (Sheet 31) and landscape details sheet (Sheet 37) reviewed for root barrier specifications. Vision analysis of Sheet 31 confirms that trees are shown throughout the site perimeter with various designations (M, SY, PL, P), but the plan notes and key notes do not include any reference to root barriers, root barrier details, or specifications for trees in proximity to utilities. Sheet 37 (Landscape Details) would typically contain root barrier detail specifications but was not examined in detail. Utility and electrical plans (Sheets 19 and 21) show transformer pad and utility locations, but no cross-reference to root barrier requirements in adjacent landscape areas.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 requires root barriers (minimum 4 feet deep, installed 5 feet from equipment) for trees within 20 lateral feet of underground electric equipment. The landscape plans show trees proposed throughout the site but provide no documentation of root barrier specifications, locations, or cross-sections demonstrating compliance with the 4-foot depth and 5-foot setback requirements. The complete absence of root barrier details, measurements, or specifications on landscape plans constitutes failure to document this requirement. Root barriers must be shown on landscape detail sheets with dimensions and cross-sections.
findings.comment: Landscape plan does not show root barrier details or specifications for trees within 20 lateral feet of transformer pad locations. Provide landscape detail drawings showing root barrier locations, dimensions (minimum 4 feet deep), installation setbacks (5 feet from transformer equipment), and materials for all trees within 20 feet of transformer pads.

applicableAreas: All proposed bike rack locations relative to transformer pads
findings.observation: Site plan (Sheet 9) notes that 41 bicycle parking spaces are provided (39 long-term in garages, 2 short-term). Construction details (Sheet 22) shows bike rack installation specifications including 3-foot minimum clearance from utilities. However, site plan drawings do not show specific bike rack locations in relation to transformer pad locations. Electrical plan (Sheet 21) shows three transformer pads but does not indicate bike rack locations. No dimensioned drawings provided showing bike rack positions relative to transformer pads.
findings.reasoning: Site planning convention requires minimum 5-foot clearance from transformer pads to bike racks. While the site plan documents total bike rack count and construction standards, it does not provide dimensioned drawings showing specific bike rack locations relative to transformer pad positions. Without a bike rack layout plan with dimensions, compliance cannot be verified.
findings.comment: Bike rack locations not dimensioned relative to transformer pads on site plan. Provide dimensioned layout showing all bike rack locations and demonstrating minimum 5-foot clearance from each transformer pad.

applicableAreas: All three transformer pad locations
findings.observation: Electrical design plan (Sheet 21) shows three transformer pads: Pad 1 (NW near Building 2), Pad 2 (SW near Building 8), and Pad 3 (central between Buildings 4, 5, 6). The pads are distributed across the western and central portions of the site. However, no dimensioned measurements are provided documenting the distances between the three transformer pads relative to each other.
findings.reasoning: Site planning convention requires minimum 5-foot clearance between transformer pads. While three pads are shown on the electrical plan, their spatial separation is not dimensionally documented. Verification of the 5-foot clearance between pads requires dimensioned measurements on the plans.
findings.comment: Distances between the three transformer pads not documented on electrical design plan. Provide dimensioned drawing showing center-to-center or edge-to-edge distances between all transformer pads, demonstrating minimum 5-foot clearance.

applicableAreas: All transformer pad locations relative to water infrastructure
findings.observation: Electrical design plan (Sheet 21) shows three transformer pad locations but does not depict water line routing or utility conflicts. Utility tap plan (Sheet 19) shows water line infrastructure (2" HDPE private domestic water branches and 6" main water lines) but does not depict transformer pad locations (transformer pads shown only on electrical sheet, not on utility sheet). While both utilities are shown on different sheets, no overlay or cross-reference plan is provided documenting distances between transformer pads and water lines.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 2.9.1.B.2 requires minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance between transformer pads and water lines. Without a coordinated drawing showing both transformer pads and water line routing simultaneously with dimensional measurements, clearances cannot be verified. The separation of transformer pads (on electrical sheet) from water infrastructure (on utility sheet) without a coordination overlay prevents documentation of compliance.
findings.comment: Transformer pad locations not coordinated with water line routing on unified plan. Provide dimensioned utility coordination drawing showing transformer pads and water lines with documented 5-foot horizontal clearances.

applicableAreas: All transformer pad locations relative to wastewater infrastructure
findings.observation: Electrical design plan (Sheet 21) shows three transformer pads but does not show wastewater line routing. Utility tap plan (Sheet 19) shows wastewater infrastructure (6" PVC wastewater branches at 2.0% minimum slope, lift station, cleanouts) but transformer pads are not depicted on this utility sheet. No overlay drawing provided showing both utilities simultaneously with dimensional clearance measurements.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 2.9.1.B.2 requires minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance between transformer pads and wastewater lines. Separation of these utilities on different sheets without a coordination drawing showing distances prevents verification of compliance.
findings.comment: Transformer pad locations not coordinated with wastewater line routing on unified plan. Provide dimensioned utility coordination drawing showing transformer pads and wastewater lines with documented 5-foot horizontal clearances.

applicableAreas: Transformer Pad 3 located in central courtyard area
findings.observation: Vision analysis of electrical design plan (Sheet 21) explicitly states: "The transformer pad symbol is drawn directly on top of an underground line labeled `SD` (Storm Drain). It is also adjacent to an underground electrical line route." This places Transformer Pad 3 directly overlapping the storm drain infrastructure shown on the electrical plan. Storm drain plan (Sheet 12) would document storm drain line routing in greater detail. Utility coordination between electrical and drainage systems is required to address this overlap.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 2.9.1.B.2 requires minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance from transformer pads to storm drain lines. The vision analysis clearly confirms that Transformer Pad 3 is positioned on top of (zero clearance from) the storm drain line marked "SD" on the electrical design plan. This represents a complete failure to maintain the required 5-foot clearance and indicates either: (1) the transformer pad location is incorrectly placed, or (2) the storm drain routing conflicts with the intended transformer pad location. This conflict must be resolved by relocating either the pad or the storm drain line.
findings.comment: Transformer Pad 3 shown directly on top of storm drain line on electrical design plan. This violates the minimum 5-foot clearance requirement. Relocate transformer pad to avoid storm drain infrastructure, or modify storm drain routing with documented approval. Provide revised electrical and drainage plans showing minimum 5-foot clearance between transformer pad edge and storm drain line.

applicableAreas: Transformer Pad 3 located over storm drain line
findings.observation: Electrical design plan (Sheet 21) shows Transformer Pad 3 positioned on top of underground storm drain line marked "SD" per vision analysis. This represents zero clearance in both horizontal and vertical dimensions from the storm drain infrastructure. UCM § 1.10.5.A requires minimum 12-inch horizontal and vertical clearance from all underground utilities except those specifically exempted (gas, fuel, steam).
findings.reasoning: The overlapping of Transformer Pad 3 on the storm drain line (SD) shown on the electrical design plan demonstrates complete failure to maintain the minimum 12-inch horizontal and vertical clearance required by UCM § 1.10.5.A. A transformer pad cannot be constructed directly over an underground storm drain line without creating structural and utility conflicts. This represents a design deficiency requiring resolution through pad relocation or utility rerouting.
findings.comment: Transformer Pad 3 overlaps underground storm drain line, providing zero clearance instead of required minimum 12 inches (horizontal and vertical). Revise design to relocate transformer pad outside of storm drain infrastructure or reroute storm drain to achieve minimum 12-inch clearance on all sides.

applicableAreas: Transformer Pad 3 located in central courtyard area
findings.observation: Vision analysis of electrical design plan (Sheet 21) confirms: "The transformer pad symbol is drawn directly on top of an underground line labeled `SD` (Storm Drain)." This indicates that Transformer Pad 3 is positioned to cross over storm drain utility infrastructure. The pad footprint (shown as a dotted rectangle) appears to be placed directly within the storm drain line routing.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.5.B prohibits locating transformer pads or Austin Energy underground facilities over or under other utility lines without written approval from the appropriate utility authority. The positioning of Transformer Pad 3 on top of the storm drain line represents a crossing/overlay configuration that violates this requirement. If utilities must cross, it requires documented written approval from both the stormwater utility (City of Austin Watershed Protection) and Austin Energy. No such approval documentation is provided in the site plan submittal.
findings.comment: Transformer Pad 3 shown positioned over storm drain line, which violates prohibition against utilities crossing without approval. Provide documentation of written approval from City of Austin Watershed Protection Department and Austin Energy Design authorizing this utility crossing, or relocate transformer pad outside storm drain infrastructure.

applicableAreas: All transformer pad locations, particularly Transformer Pad 3 in central courtyard
findings.observation: Electrical design plan (Sheet 21) shows transformer pads as simple dotted rectangles. Site plan (Sheet 9) shows general building layout without transformer detail. Grading plan (Sheet 11) shows site topography and building elevation profiles. However, no cross-section drawings or vertical clearance profiles are provided showing: (1) vertical clearances in the central courtyard area where Transformer Pad 3 is surrounded by multi-story buildings (Buildings 4, 5, 6), (2) overhead obstructions or structures above the transformer pad locations, or (3) vertical clearances for crane/equipment access.
findings.reasoning: No cross-section drawings showing vertical clearances around transformer pads are provided in the plan set. For Transformer Pad 3 especially, which is surrounded by buildings and located in a courtyard area, vertical clearance documentation is required to demonstrate that: (1) no structures hang directly above the pad, (2) adequate clearance exists for equipment maintenance and replacement, (3) proper ventilation is available if niche configuration applies, and (4) liquid drainage paths exist if oil-filled equipment.
findings.comment: Cross-section drawings not provided showing vertical clearances around transformer pads. Provide cross-section drawings through Transformer Pad 3 location demonstrating adequate vertical clearance for equipment access, maintenance, and operation; confirm no structures are positioned directly above pad.

applicableAreas: Transformer Pad 1 and Pad 2 near sidewalk/vault easements
findings.observation: Vision analysis of electrical design plan (Sheet 21) notes: "Transformer Pad 1 is located near a line labeled 'Sidewalk Easement'" and "Transformer Pad 2 is described with 'A leader line labeled "Vault Easement" points to this general area.'" Plat sheet (Sheet 2) would show recorded easements. Electrical plan indicates these easement areas but does not provide dimensional documentation showing whether the transformer pads are WITHIN the easements or merely adjacent to them. Facts.md indicates multiple easements on the property including a 7.5' Public Utility Easement, but these have not been verified against the transformer pad positions.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4 footnote 4 prohibits placing transformer pads in drainage easements, water easements, sewer easements, or electrical easements under overhead lines without written Austin Energy Design approval. The electrical plan shows pads near easement areas but does not clearly document whether pads are placed WITHIN prohibited easement zones or safely outside them. To confirm compliance, the plat and easement exhibits must be overlaid with transformer pad locations with dimensions showing either: (1) pads are completely outside all easements, or (2) if within easements, written AE Design approval is provided.
findings.comment: Transformer Pads 1 and 2 shown near sidewalk and vault easement markings on electrical design plan. Coordinate transformer pad locations with recorded easement boundaries (Plat Sheet 2 and Easement Exhibits) to verify pads are not located within prohibited drainage, water, sewer, or electrical easements. Provide dimensioned drawing showing pad locations relative to easement boundaries, or provide written Austin Energy Design approval if placement within easements is required.

applicableAreas: All three transformer pad locations
findings.observation: Electrical design plan (Sheet 21) shows three transformer pads but provides no documentation of transformer easement areas around the pads. Plat sheet (Sheet 2) and easement exhibits would show recorded easements but transformer-specific easement areas are not indicated on any plan sheets. No easement diagram or table provided showing easement widths, dimensions, or locations around the transformer pads.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires transformer easements around pads with widths determined by Austin Energy Design for accessibility and maintenance. The electrical design plan must depict transformer easement areas (typically rectangular areas extending from the pad) to demonstrate adequate space for AE personnel to access, operate, and maintain equipment. The complete absence of any easement delineation around the transformer pads represents failure to document this requirement.
findings.comment: Transformer easements not shown on electrical design plan. Provide easement exhibits showing transformer pad locations and surrounding easement areas (width and dimensions to be determined by Austin Energy Design standards) necessary for equipment accessibility and maintenance.

applicableAreas: All three transformer pad locations
findings.observation: Electrical design plan (Sheet 21) shows three transformer pads depicted only as dotted rectangular outlines with no dimensional specifications. No pad dimensions are provided (e.g., "5' x 5'", "6' x 8'"). No reference is made to Austin Energy Design-approved transformer pad detail sheets. No documentation of service type (single-phase or three-phase) appears on the electrical plan. Vision analysis confirms: pads are "depicted simply as a dotted rectangle" with no labeled dimensions or detail callouts.
findings.reasoning: The electrical plan shows transformer pad locations but provides no pad dimensions or reference to Austin Energy Design-approved specifications. Each transformer pad must be designed to AE Design standards and constructed to specific dimensions determined based on the service type and equipment to be installed. Without this documentation, the contractor would have no specifications for pad construction, and the pads may not meet AE Design requirements.
findings.comment: Transformer pad dimensions and Austin Energy Design detail references not provided on electrical design plan. For each of the three transformer pads, provide: (1) specific pad dimensions (length x width x depth); (2) confirmation of service type (single-phase or three-phase); (3) reference to applicable Austin Energy Design-approved transformer pad detail sheets; and (4) construction material and reinforcement specifications.

applicableAreas: Transformer Pad 3 located in central parking/circulation area
findings.observation: Electrical design plan (Sheet 21) shows Transformer Pad 3 positioned in the central courtyard area described as "located within an open paved/drive area surrounded by the three aforementioned buildings." Site plan (Sheet 9) shows this central area includes parking and circulation areas with driveways. Vision analysis of Sheet 21 states: "Bollards or protection barriers: None are shown or labeled." Construction details (Sheet 22) include bollard specifications per COA standards but no bollards are called out or dimensioned on the electrical plan for the transformer pad areas.
findings.reasoning: Transformer Pad 3 is positioned in the central site area that serves as a parking/circulation zone between Buildings 4, 5, and 6. This location puts the pad within the 4-foot proximity zone that triggers bollard requirements. No bollards are shown on any plan sheets protecting this pad from vehicle contact. Bollard placement and spacing must be shown on electrical/site plans to prevent accidental vehicle impact on the transformer equipment.
findings.comment: Transformer Pad 3 located in parking/circulation area without bollard protection shown. Provide detailed electrical or site plan showing 4-inch minimum diameter galvanized rigid metal bollards positioned around Transformer Pad 3 to prevent vehicle contact. Bollard spacing must allow pad access door to open fully per Austin Energy Design equipment pad standards.
